protocol: 3 rounds x 3 proposals; one positive scoring winner at most per round

descriptor_candidates.name: confined_free_volume_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss scales with the balance of accessible volume to pore-wall surface: adsorbates in pores with high Vol/(ASA·pore-diameter) ratio retain more translational freedom, so s_ads/s_gas increases with this descriptor; the network will predict lower entropy loss for higher values.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from confinement theory: adsorption entropy loss is dominated by loss of translational degrees of freedom, governed by the ratio of free volume to confining surface area per pore dimension. Vol and LabuteASA capture zeolite geometry; lsd_p rescales per pore channel. Source evidence: none supplied; this is physical reasoning only.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R is not reduced relative to the 14-input baseline, or if residual analysis shows no monotonic trend of entropy loss with this descriptor within pore-size regimes, the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: anisotropy_shape_descriptor
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Molecular/zeolite anisotropy (moment-of-geometry asymmetry) combined with the smallest enclosing dimension controls orientational entropy loss: systems with high anisotropy confine rotational modes more strongly, increasing entropy loss beyond what size alone predicts.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Rotational restriction in narrow or slit-like channels depends on the shape anisotropy of the confining geometry; PMI ratios encode elongation/disc-ness, PBF the minimum projection width. This re-expresses existing shape information in an orientation-sensitive form. Source evidence: none supplied; mechanism is inferred.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if adding this nonlinearly transformed descriptor does not improve MAE of entropy loss/R over baseline, or if the residual correlation sign contradicts the predicted direction across straight vs. cage-type channels.

descriptor_candidates.name: packing_tightness_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss peaks at intermediate packing tightness: the exponential of (accessible volume × framework volume) normalized by characteristic framework lengths measures how snugly the adsorbate-zeolite pair packs; too tight (vibration-dominated) or too loose (retained translation) reduces loss, so the descriptor improves prediction of the non-monotonic entropy-loss regime.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mixed translational-vibrational confinement models predict non-monotonic entropy loss with packing density; combining volumetric (AV, Vol) and length-scale (lsd_f, GeDi, SPAN) quantities into an exponential tightness index gives the network a smooth intermediate-maximum feature. Source evidence: none supplied; inference only. Density deliberately excluded to avoid unverified unit assignment.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if MAE of entropy loss/R does not decrease versus baseline, or if entropy loss is monotonically related to the descriptor in the test set, contradicting the intermediate-tightness mechanism.

descriptor_candidates.name: confinement_aspect_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is governed by the dimensional mismatch between framework-limiting and pore-limiting lengths, normalized by framework volume per accessible volume: systems where the framework-pore length contrast is large relative to molecular span compress translational modes anisotropically, so entropy loss (in units of R) increases with this descriptor; the network will assign higher entropy loss to large values.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from anisotropic confinement theory: when framework and pore length scales differ, adsorbates lose translational freedom directionally; the Vol/(AV·density) term (all zeolite-native scales) rescales the length contrast by bulk/accessible volume. No source evidence supplied; this is physical reasoning only, not a verified literature relation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if MAE of entropy loss/R does not improve over the 14-input baseline (current best 0.5412), or if residual analysis shows the descriptor is redundant with retained confined_free_volume_ratio (near-collinear residuals).

descriptor_candidates.name: vibrational_coupling_index
descriptor_candidates.formula: exp(-1.0 * MW / (ASA * abs(PBF))) * log(1.0 + density * lsd_f ** 2)
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss contains a vibrational contribution controlled by adsorbate mass per confining surface: heavy adsorbates in high-surface-area, narrow-frame (small PBF) pores have low-frequency hindered modes and lose more entropy (higher entropy loss/R); the exponential coupling index captures this mass–surface regime that pure geometric ratios miss.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from harmonic-oscillator entropy scaling: vibrational entropy loss grows with mass and tightness of confinement. Combining MW (adsorbate) with ASA and PBF (framework) yields a mass-per-wall metric; the log-density-length term adds framework rigidity scale using the source numerical density scale without assigned units. Source evidence: none supplied; mechanism inferred.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if MAE of entropy loss/R does not decrease relative to baseline, or if splitting the test set by MW shows the descriptor does not reduce error preferentially in the heavy-adsorbate (high-MW) regime.

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_moment_efficiency
descriptor_candidates.formula: minimum(PMI1, PMI2, PMI3) ** 0.5 / (LabuteASA * GeDi) + 0.5 * (SPAN / maximum(lsd_f, lsd_p)) ** 2
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is minimized when the smallest geometric moment of the accessible surface is large relative to the confining length scale: bulky, compactly confined adsorbates (large minimum PMI per surface-area-length product, and molecular span exceeding the larger limiting pore diameter) retain rotational entropy, so the descriptor marks a low-entropy-loss regime the network can exploit as a regime switch.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from statistical mechanics of confined rotors: rotational entropy loss depends on the smallest principal moment relative to the accessible surface geometry; the SPAN-to-limiting-diameter ratio flags when molecular span exceeds all pore dimensions (total confinement). Source evidence: none supplied; mechanism inferred, not a documented relation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if MAE of entropy loss/R fails to improve over baseline, or if the predicted sign (high descriptor → lower entropy loss) is not observed in residual stratification between small-PMI and large-PMI adsorbate subsets.

descriptor_candidates.name: translational_release_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Adsorption entropy loss (in units of R) decreases with the ratio of accessible framework volume to confining wall area per framework length, modulated by how much accessible volume fits within the adsorbate's geometric envelope: pores that offer more free volume per wall contact relative to the molecule's span preserve translational degrees of freedom, so s_ads/s_gas rises with this descriptor and the network should predict smaller entropy loss at high values.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from lattice/transition-state confinement theory: translational entropy loss scales with the number of sites accessible per confining dimension; the square-root volume-per-wall term (Vol/ASA/lsd_f) is a confinement length, and AV/(SPAN*GeDi) rescales it against the adsorbate's own dimensional envelope. Distinct from retained confined_free_volume_ratio by using per-gram ASA and framework length lsd_f and by adding the molecular-envelope normalization. Source evidence: none supplied; this is physical reasoning only.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if MAE of entropy loss/R does not fall below the retained best 0.5412, or if residual analysis shows high-descriptor systems do not exhibit systematically lower entropy loss after controlling for pore size (no monotonic trend within lsd_p strata).

descriptor_candidates.name: inertial_wall_loading
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss grows with adsorbate mass loading per unit confining wall area, rescaled by the intermediate principal moment: heavy adsorbates confined in high-surface-area, low-moment (slit-like or narrow) pores experience strongly hindered modes and lose more entropy, so the exponential term saturates near 1 (low loss regime) for light/large-moment systems and the network predicts higher entropy loss at larger values of MW*density/(PMI2*ASA); the added squared pore-to-span ratio flags near-complete geometric confinement.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from hindered-rotor/oscillator entropy scaling: characteristic frequencies of confined modes scale as sqrt(k/m_eff), so mass per confining area with an effective moment-of-geometry denominator controls the vibrational/rotational entropy loss. Unlike the round-2 vibrational_coupling_index, this uses PMI2 (a rotational-scaled moment) and a dimensionless pore/span confinement flag instead of PBF and a density-length term. Source evidence: none supplied; mechanism inferred.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if MAE of entropy loss/R does not improve over 0.5412, or if stratifying test residuals by MW shows no preferential error reduction in the high-MW regime, or if the descriptor's correlation with the retained volume-ratio descriptor is so high (|r|>0.95) that it adds no information.

descriptor_candidates.name: elongation_pressure_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is largest when molecular elongation (PMI3/PMI1) coincides with a pore diameter smaller than the molecular span and low free-volume redundancy per accessible volume: elongated molecules in tight, low-redundancy pores lose rotational and orientational entropy nonlinearly, so entropy loss/R increases with the logarithmic elongation-pressure index; this provides the network an interaction regime (elongation x confinement x free-volume scarcity) that individual size and shape features cannot express.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from configurational entropy of rod-like confined adsorbates: orientational freedom collapses when the smallest confining dimension approaches the molecular span, and the effect is amplified when there is little excess accessible volume per unit accessible-volume scale. All three factors (elongation, span-to-pore ratio, volumetric redundancy) interact multiplicatively, hence the log-compressed product form. Source evidence: none supplied; mechanism is inferred, not a documented literature relation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if MAE of entropy loss/R fails to beat 0.5412, or if residual analysis shows the predicted interaction (steep entropy-loss increase only when SPAN/lsd_p > 1 AND PMI3/PMI1 is high) is absent in the test set, or if the descriptor performs identically when the elongation factor is replaced by a constant (indicating the interaction is not real).
